result:
Everything's in place and verified. Here's the summary:

## What was wrong
This SaaS pivoted from "InboxZap" (email cleanup) to "Lumina" (AI meeting assistant), but the pivot was never finished in the code:
- Every page's `<title>`/description/OG tags still said "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes" while the content was about Lumina — a branded-query click-through would land on a totally unrelated page.
- The only content that ranked (12 blog posts, ~14k monthly impressions) was about email cleanup/inbox zero — irrelevant to the new product, and already stuck at position 40-60 with near-zero CTR.
- `/features` and `/pricing` were linked everywhere but didn't exist as routes.
- `/blog` was a client component fetching `/api/posts`, an endpoint that doesn't exist — no server-rendered content at all for crawlers.
- The sitemap had a literal `TODO` and never included blog posts.
- `/faq` redirected to `/#faq`, but there was no `#faq` section on the homepage.

## What I changed
- `app/layout.tsx` — fixed metadata to match the real product, added a title template.
- `app/features/page.tsx`, `app/pricing/page.tsx` — built the missing routes.
- `lib/posts.ts` + `app/blog/page.tsx` + `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` — replaced the broken client-fetch blog with statically-generated pages (verified in `next build` output) and real per-post metadata, now targeting keywords tied to what Lumina actually sells (meeting notes, action items, transcription, async standups, meeting overload) instead of the old inbox-zero niche.
- `app/sitemap.ts` — now dynamically includes every real page and post.
- `app/page.tsx` — added a real FAQ section with `id="faq"` and FAQPage JSON-LD, so the existing redirect resolves to something and picks up rich-result eligibility.
- `next.config.js` — 301s the 12 legacy `/blog/post-N` URLs to `/blog` instead of leaving them as dead ends under the new brand.

Verified with `next build` (all routes compile and prerender) and `next start` + curl (titles, redirects, sitemap, and internal links all resolve correctly).

One unrelated thing worth flagging: `npm install` reported `next@14.2.5` has a known security vulnerability (critical) — worth a dependency bump when you get a chance, separate from this SEO work.
